days.title: Ask for Them by Name (Even Without the Name)
days.scripture_text: Ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you.
days.prayer: Lord, I am asking plainly: bring me my spouse. You already know their name, their face, their fears, their laugh. Bless them today, wherever they are. Guard their faith and their heart, and set our paths toward each other in Your time. Amen.
days.reflection: PLACEHOLDER — final text by Ryan & wife. Theme: bold, specific petition is not presumption; the Gospel invites asking.
days.closing: St. Raphael, companion of travelers, guide us to each other.

days.title: Praying for a Stranger You Already Love
days.scripture_text: For I know the thoughts that I think towards you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of affliction, to give you an end and patience.
days.prayer: Father, my future spouse is having an ordinary day somewhere right now. Whatever they carry today — stress, doubt, a hard conversation, a small victory — be close to them. Let my prayer reach where I cannot. Amen.
days.reflection: PLACEHOLDER — final text by Ryan & wife. Theme: the strange sweetness of loving someone you haven't met; intercession as the first act of the marriage.
days.closing: Our Lady, keep them under your mantle.

days.title: Be Findable
days.scripture_text: He that hath found a good wife, hath found a good thing, and shall receive a pleasure from the Lord.
days.prayer: Lord, seeking is not only praying — it is showing up. Give me the courage to be present where good people gather: the parish, the young-adult night, the pizza before Mass. Free me from the fear of being seen. Amen.
days.reflection: PLACEHOLDER — final text by Ryan & wife. Theme: cooperation with grace; community, showing up, Pizza-to-Pews energy — contemporary and practical without being a dating manual.
days.closing: St. Anne, who raised the Mother of God, pray for us.
